events.content:
Done — category links now runtime-prefetch their full URL-specific content, so clicking navigates instantly from the client cache without the "Loading category..." fallback or a server render at click time. The `/catalog?category=...` URLs are unchanged.

Two-line change, leaning on this app's already-enabled `cacheComponents` support for runtime prefetching:

- `lib/data.ts` — added `'use cache'` to `getProducts`. Since `category` is an argument, each category gets its own cache entry, and cached content is allowed to resolve inside a per-URL prefetch (a runtime prefetch knows the target URL, so `searchParams` resolves there too — no restructuring of `CategoryResults` needed).
- `app/page.tsx` — added `prefetch={true}` to each category `Link`, upgrading it from the default static-shell prefetch (which stops at the Suspense boundary) to a full runtime prefetch of that exact URL when the link enters the viewport.

Verified against a production build (`next build` passes, `/catalog` shows as Partial Prerender):

- Simulating the router's runtime-prefetch request (`RSC: 1`, `Next-Router-Prefetch: 2`) for `?category=sale` returns a payload already containing the "Products on sale" heading and "Canvas Tote"/"Travel Mug"; `?category=featured` returns "Featured products" with "Desk Lamp"/"Wool Blanket" — each URL's content is fully prepared before any click, so navigation never waits on the 800 ms fetch.
- A warm prefetch answers in ~20 ms (cache hit), and a direct hard load of `/catalog?category=sale` still streams correctly.

Note the `tsconfig.json` diff is just `next build` auto-updating it (jsx runtime, include paths), and `package.json` was already modified before I started.
